title: Ballast processor seems to escape virtual memory and enter RSS
body:
### Component(s)

_No response_

### What happened?

## Description
Open telemetry agent goes around utilising over 6Gb of memory while scraping merely 6-7 pods on the node. 

## Steps to Reproduce
Use the provided configuration. 

## Expected Result
In agent mode, it should ideally use less than 1Gi memory to run smoothly on the agent

## Actual Result
Uses over 6Gi memory at times. Have cases where it even crosses 64Gi memory if the node has that level of memory available. Looks like GC never runs

### Collector version

0.69.0

### Environment information

## Environment
OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04")
Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2")


### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration


comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Memory ballast got it under control. Without memory ballast it was reaching 12Gi if the node had that amount of memory available. 

Also wouldn't memory ballast consume 33% what is available? We have about 500 other agents running, all sitting well below 2Gi - there are agents running on even larger nodes but still the consumption is not this high.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 One more thing we observed today is - memory heap graph shoes high consumption for memory ballast even for the pods that are using practically low memory looking at the metrics. These pods reside on nodes which do have sufficient memory available for memory ballast to get hold of. My question here would be - How does memory ballast really function (if you are aware of it). Does it reserve the desired memory or just tries to capture until available?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: https://blog.twitch.tv/en/2019/04/10/go-memory-ballast-how-i-learnt-to-stop-worrying-and-love-the-heap/ explains the mechanics of a memory ballast generally.  Look to the implementation for details.  It basically[ makes a big slice](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/extension/ballastextension/memory_ballast.go#L48-L50) and then never uses it.  That slice stays in virtual memory, so if you're looking at RSS you will not see the impact of the ballast there.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: That's what I'd expect but unfortunately not the case. That is exactly the reason why I'm confused about what's happening. To my surprise, even after setting memory ballast to exactly 1024Mib in size, some pods still show memory usage around 200-500MiB and same trend for memory.rss too One on the left is memory.usage while one on the right is memory.rss

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: That's a plausible explanation.  I believe we've recently discussed whether the ballast extension is even needed with the availability of `GOMEMLIMIT`.  Are you able to set an appropriate limit and `GOGC` value and remove the ballast, as suggested [here](https://weaviate.io/blog/gomemlimit-a-game-changer-for-high-memory-applications#gomemlimit--no-more-need-for-a-workaround)?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: For what it's worth, we observed the same thing in kuberentes.  otel using many gigs of memory in RSS.  We recommend others reading this ticket to turn off the memory ballast in otel.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Not sure if this adds any value as the issue is quite old...

I've done quite a lot of fiddling around with the memory_ballast extension and the memory_limiter processor, trying one with without the other, both the same time, different values in each, same values for each etc... and I've observed a lot of weird, unexplainable behaviour regarding VSZ & RSS. I can almost never predict what the memory usage is going to be if I'm honest - not even a ballpark range, it always feels totally random to me.

Actually the primary reason I found this issue is I wanted to understand where I was lacking knowledge, so I could attempt to predict my collectors memory usage. It's good to know it's not just me experiencing these issues.

I've found recently that when I disable the ballast extension, the memory usage of my collector is lower and importantly, more predictable. I don't know if I'm sacrificing any performance under heavier load though.

My next steps over the coming weeks is to drop the ballast entirely, and use GOMEMLIMIT instead, as has been hinted here and elsewhere. I will need to understand how it differs from the memory_limiter processor though, as that is not currently obvious to me.
